matched: Both statistical regression models and machine learning models were employed to develop predictive models for membrane fouling (linear vs non-linear patterns)
Linear regression models relationship between dependent variable Y and independent variables Xi assuming linear relationship (Eq. 3)
Lasso regression adds L1 regularization penalty to shrink coefficients to zero, performing feature selection and mitigating overfitting (Eq. 4)
Ridge regression incorporates L2 regularization to penalize large coefficients, address multicollinearity, and reduce model variance (Eq. 5)
Elastic net regression combines L1 and L2 penalties via hyperparameter alpha, effective for high-dimensional datasets with correlated features (Eq. 6)

Machine learning multi-stage workflow: Input (preprocessed features F/M, MLSS, moving averages), Training (iterative decision trees minimizing prediction error and penalizing overfitting), Output (specific flux directly quantifying fouling severity), Interpretation (SHAP values providing actionable levers)

Overfitting prevention strategies: 5-fold cross-validation, Early stopping based on validation loss for CatBoost and XGBoost, Hyperparameter tuning via grid search, Model complexity control (max tree depth and min child weight)
XGBoost is an optimized tree-based boosting algorithm designed for parallel computation and enhanced model efficiency (Eq. 7)
CatBoost developed by Yandex handles categorical features and mitigates prediction shift through ordered boosting with regularization term R_ordered(D) (Eq. 8)
